title: Hadith on Faith and Contentment
summary: The Prophet emphasized faith in Allah and contentment as virtues, warning against greed and worldliness.
translation: In the Hadith, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) stated that the first virtue of this Ummah is to have faith in Allah and to adopt asceticism and contentment. The first corruption of this Ummah is greed and extending desires in the world. The essence of the Hadith is that the good and success in religion and the Hereafter depend on Taqwa (piety), which is achieved through asceticism and certainty. The root of corruption in religion and the Hereafter is greed and evil desires, which are born from stinginess and the desire for a long life in the world. When one has complete faith and certainty in Allah as the Provider, the corrupting substance of stinginess does not spread in a person's mind, because the cause of stinginess is the uncertainty that overcomes one concerning sustenance. This leads to various thoughts, such as worrying that if one spends their wealth in the path of Allah right now, then where will they eat from tomorrow. Similarly, when a person adopts asceticism, the desire to stay in the world or wish for a long life disappears. Hence, it is said in this Hadith that this Ummah's first corruption is greed and desire because these two traits go against the belief in Allah as the Provider and asceticism. Therefore, scholars have written that a person should always live with contentment with little and belief in Allah as the Provider. The benefit of this is that a person can get by with little and is never left without sustenance. The summary and the meaning of the Hadith that comes forth is that a person should always have faith in Allah, and live their life with asceticism and disinterest in wealth; one should not have excessive greed, ambition, or stinginess.
